newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit at standstill despite bullish dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit at standstill despite bullish dollar.

text.p: The ringgit was at a virtual standstill despite the dollar's surge against the mark, dealers said.
Ringgit profit-taking after its late Monday's surge helped the dollar to gain some ground, but it was otherwise kept to a boxed range, they said.
"People are mixed on where the ringgit is going. That's why it didn't move much," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
The dollar rose to a near three-year high against the mark in Tokyo, rising as high as 1.7050 marks. It rose further in European dealings.
Dealers said the dollar's continued strength later on Tuesday could depress the ringgit.
Speculation of a hike in Malaysia's statutory reserve requirement (SRR) which would boost interest rates, provided some support for the ringgit.
But interbank dealers said the central bank was unlikely to hike the SRR above the current 13.5 percent level and would be more keen to keep interest rates steady.
At the Kuala Lumpur close at 1000 GMT, ringgit was at 2.4786/91 a dollar from 2.4858/65 at Monday's close.
